name: Mongolia
summary: The modern state of Mongolia, which declared independence from the Qing in 1911, became a Soviet-aligned people’s republic (1924–1990) and is now a parliamentary democracy.

knownFor.label: Naadam festival
knownFor.note: Wrestling, horse racing and archery each July.

knownFor.label: Ger (yurt)
knownFor.note: Many families still live in round felt tents.

location.value: Between Russia and China; about 1.56 million km², landlocked.

terrain.value: Steppe, the Gobi Desert, the Altai and Khangai mountains.

climate.value: Extremely continental: very cold winters, short summers.

resources.value: Grassland for herds, copper, gold, coal.

disasters.value: Dzud: harsh winters that kill millions of animals.

population.value: About 3.5 million today, one of the least densely populated countries.

disease.value: Winter air pollution in Ulaanbaatar from coal stoves harms health.

migration.value: Many herders have moved to the capital after harsh winters (dzud) killed livestock.

wealth.value: A lower-middle-income country, with a mining boom that raised incomes in the 2010s.

inequality.value: Gaps between the capital and the countryside.

governmentType.value: A Buddhist theocracy (1911–24), a one-party socialist state (1924–90), now a semi-presidential republic.

keyRulers.value: Bogd Khan (1911–24). Khorloogiin Choibalsan (in power from 1928; died 1952). Yumjaagiin Tsedenbal (1952–84).

succession.value: Multi-party elections have been held since 1990.

institutions.value: The State Great Khural (parliament) and a directly elected president.

stability.value: Purges in the 1930s killed tens of thousands, including many monks.

eliteConflict.value: Party competition has been intense, with debates over mining deals and corruption.

armyAndTech.value: A small army; Soviet troops were stationed until the early 1990s.

majorWars.value: The Battles of Khalkhin Gol (1939) with Soviet forces against Japan.

territoryChange.value: Independence recognised by China in 1946; mutual recognition with the PRC on 6 October 1949.

alliancesRivals.value: Allied with the Soviet Union until 1990; now balances Russia and China.

inventions.value: No major inventions in modern times; the Naadam festival and horse-riding culture are well known.

scienceEducation.value: Literacy has been very high since Soviet times.

openness.value: Closed to the West until 1990, and now open to trade and investment.

communicationTransport.value: The Trans-Mongolian Railway (1956); long distances by jeep and horse.

languageWriting.value: Mongolian, written in Cyrillic since the 1940s; the traditional script is being revived.

artsArchitecture.value: Throat singing, the horse-head fiddle (morin khuur).

socialStructure.value: Herders and city dwellers; about half the people live in Ulaanbaatar.

sharedIdentity.value: Strong identity tied to Genghis Khan and nomadic life.

dailyLife.value: Gers on the steppe and in city ger districts; meat, dairy, milk tea.

neighbours.value: Russia to the north and China to the south, with no sea access.

ideasReligions.value: Communism until 1990, then democracy; Tibetan Buddhism has revived.

colonisation.value: Part of the Qing Empire until 1911.

riseSignals.value: Independence after the fall of the Qing (1911).

peakPeriod.value: A mining boom in the 2010s, driven by copper and coal.

declineSignals.value: Dependence on mining and on China as the main buyer.

outcome.value: Mongolia continues as an independent state.
